markup.message: lt-error-summary is on <div>, and belongs on <lt-error-summary>. Write <lt-error-summary class="lt-error-summary">.

page.message:
for="budget-help" points at a

, which cannot have a label. for must point at the field itself: ,

The help text is not wired to any field: its id "budget-help" is not in aria-describedby on any field. A screen reader does not announce it together with the field. Write that id in aria-describedby on the field, or put the field and the text in <lt-field>, which wires them in the browser. If the code that renders the markup can call a builder function, lt.field({ id, help: true }) or Lt.field(id = ..., help = true) writes both the id and aria-describedby.

The error text is not wired to any field: it has no id, so no aria-describedby can point at it. A screen reader does not announce it together with the field. Write an id on the text and the same id in aria-describedby on the field, or put the field and the text in <lt-field>, which wires them in the browser. If the code that renders the markup can call a builder function, lt.field({ id, error: true, invalid: true }) or Lt.field(id = ..., error = true, invalid = true) writes both the id and aria-describedby.
lt-error-summary is on <div>, and belongs on <lt-error-summary>. Write <lt-error-summary class="lt-error-summary">.
The link in the error summary goes to "#the-budget", which does not exist on the page. It must go to the field that failed, so the user lands where the error can be fixed.

The error text is not wired to any field: it has no id, so no aria-describedby can point at it. A screen reader does not announce it together with the field. Write an id on the text and the same id in aria-describedby on the field, or put the field and the text in <lt-field>, which wires them in the browser. If the code that renders the markup can call a builder function, lt.field({ id, warning: true }) or Lt.field(id = ..., warning = true) writes both the id and aria-describedby.
